_comment: Illustrative example for schema documentation only. All numbers, dates and claims are placeholders, not real data or research.
executive_summary: Late-cycle disinflation: tilt toward defensive growth, keep quality.
Health care is the main expansion; one BUY proposal (MRK) passed every rule.
Staples and financials trimmed toward macro mid-bands; JPM trimmed by CIO override.
IT stays two points above the macro cap to avoid selling core funds at a taxable gain.

reconciliation.topic: Reduce financials vs JPM HOLD verdict
reconciliation.phase1_position: Reduce financials from 25% to 23% of the portfolio.
reconciliation.findings: The financials sector head rated JPM HOLD on rules; conviction 6.1 and evidence 7.0.
reconciliation.resolution: Trim JPM by the amount needed to reach the 23% target; thesis unchanged.

reconciliation.findings: Phase 3 produced one BUY (MRK) with rr 2.7 and DA verdict survives.
reconciliation.resolution: Initiate MRK at the standard 3% starter size; remaining gap stays in cash.

final_actions.override_justification: Financials sit two points above the CIO target and JPM is the largest single position in the sector, so a partial trim is the cleanest way to close the gap.
final_actions.note: Size set by portfolio.py breach sizing.

constraint_overrides.justification: IT exposure comes almost entirely from the QQQ and SPMO core funds; cutting it by two points would mean selling a core fund at a taxable gain, so the excess is tolerated and reviewed next run.

top_risks: A growth scare would hit financials and the IT-heavy funds together.
KO's open tax case could pressure dividend coverage.
Fund overlap concentrates exposure in a handful of mega-cap names.
dissent_summary: The operator lens argued for higher KO conviction; the technical lens flagged weak relative strength in staples. The DA damaged KO's thesis but did not break it. No dissent changed a final action.
conviction_reason: Most findings agree with the phase 1 direction; sizing is conservative.
